name: genext2fs
desc: Generates an ext2 filesystem as a normal (non-root) user
why: Builds ext2 filesystem images without root, a neat door into how filesystems are laid out on disk.

brief.what_it_is: genext2fs is a command-line tool that generates an ext2 filesystem image as an ordinary non-root user. It writes the image file directly, so you do not mount it to copy files in. It can also create device nodes and set user and group IDs without being superuser. The homepage does not describe its exact inputs or flags, and no commands appear on the page.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a way to build ext2 images without root, since normally that needs mounting the image or being superuser. The author's words: "It doesn't require you to mount the image file to copy files on it."
brief.install_notes: The homepage says most Linux distributions already package genext2fs. For bugfixes and newer features, it says to get the source from GitHub and build it yourself. The GitHub URL was not given as a link in the text I received, so I did not follow it. Homebrew installs the executable named genext2fs.
brief.standout: Building a filesystem image without mounting it or using root is the unusual part. It makes a small, readable window into how ext2 lays out inodes, blocks and device nodes on disk.
brief.status: Quiet. The homepage says "the project is kind of hibernating right now." I found no release date or commit history because the GitHub repository was not fetched.
brief.caveats: The homepage is very thin and gives no usage examples, supported options, or platform details. Bug reports go through an issue tracker that the homepage links to but whose address I could not read. The project is described as hibernating, so expect slow fixes. I could not confirm the GitHub source location from the homepage text alone.
quotes: Simply, it generates an ext2 filesystem as a normal (i.e. non-root) user.
It doesn't require you to mount the image file to copy files on it.
the project is kind of hibernating right now.
